To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
it is possible, but not easy, to record brain dynamics during movement and that it is possible but not easy to record body dynamics during movement.

(1) EEG can be recorded and analyzed synchronously with body dynamics during motion; (2) the most suitable recording systems are wireless; (3) the most suitable electrode caps are dry; (4) the most suitable electrodes are dry and gel; (5) real/custom electrode positions can be determined by a variety of methods.
it is possible and feasible to measure and analyze brain and body dynamics during motion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a methodological framework to measure body dynamics and brain dynamics during movement and exercise tasks.
methodological solutions that enable the recording, analysis and interpretation of brain and body dynamics during movement or exercise.
how to measure the brain and body during movement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are many ways to measure EEG, EMG and body dynamics during movement and it is up to the investigator which one to choose, based on the research question.

there are many solutions and techniques that have been suggested in order to record brain and body dynamics during motion, but the best solution is to combine several techniques in order to obtain a more accurate and complete picture of the dynamics of both the brain and body.
the recording of brain and body dynamics during motion is possible and that it is a growing research area.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the methodological aspects of EEG during motion are well developed.
the combination of EEG, EMG and kinematic data can be used for the study of motor control and motor learning, and for the development of brain-computer interfaces.
it is possible and feasible to measure brain and body dynamics in a synchronized manner during motion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a combination of different recording systems, electrodes, and techniques can be used to record and analyze brain and body dynamics during motion.
the recording of brain dynamics during movement is feasible.
the methodological difficulties that are associated with the measurement of body and brain dynamics can be solved and overcome.
